In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the pattern of synaptic organization in the pallidal complex is more complex than previously thought, and that the synaptic organization of GPe differs significantly from that of GPi.
the synaptic innervations of perikarya and dendritic shafts of neurons in GPe and in GPi by GABA‐ and/or glutamate‐contaning terminals differ in several aspects.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
GPe is mainly innervated by the striatal terminals, while GPi receives a major contribution from the GPe terminals.
, in GPe, the striatal terminals form most of the axosomatc synapses, whereas, in GPi, the GPe terminals are the most prominent.
GPe is mainly innervated by the striatal GABA‐containing terminals, whereas GPi is predominantly innervated by GPe GABAergic terminals.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the synaptic innervations of perikarya and dendritic shafts of neurons in GPe and Gpi are markedly different, suggesting that the two segments of the pallidum may have different functional roles.
the pattern of synaptic input received by pallidal neurons is different in the two pallidal segments.
the pattern of synaptic inputs to perikarya in the GPe and GPI is different.
